items.title: After Editing Two AI-Assisted Manuscripts, I Rewrote My Client Agreement
items.excerpt: A freelance editor describes what AI-assisted manuscripts actually look like on the page and why they cost more to fix. She rewrote her client agreement to add AI-disclosure terms and a surcharge for heavily generated drafts.

items.title: News Summary: AI-Generated Stories Outperform Human Writing in Reader Ratings
items.excerpt: A Villanova University study finds readers largely cannot tell AI-generated short fiction from human-written work, and often rate the AI stories higher. ALLi unpacks what that means for indie authors' disclosure and craft decisions.

items.title: Reading Between the Lines, Part 2: Cognitive Debt and the Adaptive Publisher
items.excerpt: The central risk of AI in publishing is framed not as hallucination but as "cognitive debt" — the gradual erosion of the human judgement that gives writing its originality and integrity. Part 2 sets out how an adaptive publisher should design workflows to pay that debt down.

items.title: Reading Between the Lines, Part 1: A Cognitive Framework for AI in Scholarly Publishing
items.excerpt: Part 1 argues AI is now permanent in publishing and the open question is how it should be understood and governed. It offers a cognitive framework mapping where AI mediation helps and where it displaces editorial judgement.

items.title: News Podcast: Literary Agents Update Ethics Rules; Seven-Figure Deal Shelved Over AI Claims
items.excerpt: Dan Holloway covers US agents rewriting their ethics guidelines for AI-era submissions, a seven-figure deal shelved over AI allegations, and a new peer-reviewed study of AI-made books on Amazon.

items.title: McGraw Hill Touts AI in Improving First Quarter Results
items.excerpt: CEO Philip Moyer called AI "a genuine tailwind for our business" as the educational publisher reported higher sales and earnings, crediting AI-built study and courseware products. (PW publishes no machine-readable timestamp; byline date Aug 13, 2026, clock time approximated.)

items.title: Claude's new Scarlet Letter watermark is invisible—for now
items.excerpt: Anthropic's new text watermark flags anything Claude touched, including human writing the model only edited. For writers and editors that turns light AI assistance into a permanently detectable mark on the manuscript.

items.title: Europe's New AI Rules Are Reaching Authors Worldwide | Self-Publishing News (Aug. 13, 2026)
items.excerpt: Dale Roberts walks indie authors through EU AI transparency rules now reaching Claude users worldwide, plus a new study challenging assumptions about AI-written fiction. Practical read on what authors must disclose and when.

items.title: The web's newest weapon against AI scrapers is a font
items.excerpt: "ShieldFont" scrambles text for AI training crawlers while staying perfectly readable to humans. It's a typographic defence writers and publishers can apply to serialized fiction, samples, and newsletter archives.

items.title: Going Indie, Publishing Innovation, And The Challenges Of Book Marketing With John Bond
items.excerpt: Joanna Penn and publishing consultant John Bond discuss where real innovation in book production and marketing is happening now, and why it keeps emerging from the indie side rather than the big houses.

items.title: Links of Interest: August 12, 2026
items.excerpt: Jane Friedman's industry digest: publishers don't fact-check memoir, HarperCollins' CEO calls for industry-wide AI-authorship solutions, and more on how AI is reshaping trade publishing practice.

items.title: Why Smart Authors Aren't Worried About AI
items.excerpt: Jason Hamilton argues the authors thriving right now treat AI as a production tool inside a human-led process, and breaks down which parts of the writing workflow actually benefit from automation.

items.title: Shueisha's New Global Manga Platform Found Using AI Translation Despite Publisher Claiming It Doesn't
items.excerpt: Shueisha's 100th-anniversary platform Manga Million offers 1M pages in 100+ languages, and readers found AI translation artifacts despite the publisher insisting real people did the work. A live test of machine translation in comics publishing. (Off-list source: no allowed_domain outlet covered this story in-window.)

items.title: The Published Voice: Whose Voice Are We Really Reading?
items.excerpt: If AI drafts, smooths, and translates an author's prose, what happens to "author voice" — long a core criterion for reviewers and editors? The piece asks how much mediation a published voice can absorb before it stops being the author's.

items.title: News Summary: A Tale of Two Seven-Figure Deals (and the Response to AI Allegations)
items.excerpt: Two seven-figure book deals hit AI-use allegations and the publishers responded in opposite ways — one stood by its author, the other walked away. A look at how the trade is improvising an AI-provenance standard.

items.title: Princeton University Press Partners with Cashmere on AI Licensing
items.excerpt: Princeton joins Rockefeller University Press and Springer in using the Cashmere licensing platform to make catalogs available to copyright-compliant, non-LLM AI products. (PW exposes no machine-readable timestamp; byline date Aug 03, 2026, clock time approximated.)

items.title: Writer introduces new AI model and upgraded harness to contain token costs
items.excerpt: Writer ships a new model plus an agent harness aimed at keeping long-form generation costs predictable. Relevant to anyone running book-length or catalog-scale text production on LLMs.
